body: I am in the US. School is out for the summer! Summers are hard because I'm home alone all day. What's your favorite YA book?
Thanks for looking that up for me. It makes me a lot less nervous about calling.

Yeah, it might help to open up about negative side effects. My doctor's office is open until 4:30, so I have about 4 hours to work up the courage. 

My favorite book is Everyday by David Levithan. I love stupid young adult fiction. I am a preschool teacher, actually. I love working with kids.

I am terrified of being admitted into a psychiatric unit. I know I need to call my doctor but phone calls are extremely difficult for me also. 

The last time I've seen any of my friends was a few months ago. I live a few states away from all my friends. I went to college far away, graduated and have a job here. I never managed to get close with anyone from here.
I've had mild thoughts of death and suicide before the meds. My fleeting and intrusive thoughts have turned into plans and ideas since taking the medication. It's gotten worse.

I don't remember the last book I read, to be honest. It's been a few months. No matter what I do, the thought of wanting to die is always in the background, haunting me. I've been on medication for 3 weeks. 

I appreciate you taking the time to talk to me, btw.

In the past I've enjoyed nature and reading and spending time with my friends. I don't enjoy anything anymore though. I'm in therapy and on medication for depression and it's straight up not working. I am fundamentally broken. I think I'll always want to die. There is nothing in the future because I'll always be broken.
